title: Find Three Consecutive Equal Values
learning_objective: Learn how to detect when the same number appears in the previous, current, and next rows.

tutorial.explanation: A value appears three times consecutively when a middle row has the same value as both its previous row and its next row. LAG and LEAD make that comparison direct.
tutorial.syntax: WITH neighbors AS (SELECT num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs) SELECT DISTINCT num FROM neighbors WHERE num = prev_num AND num = next_num;
tutorial.mental_model: Think of each row as the possible center of a three-row streak. If both neighbors match it, the streak exists.

guided_example.prompt: Find numbers that appear in at least one three-row streak.
guided_example.solution_query: WITH neighbors AS (SELECT num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs) SELECT DISTINCT num AS consecutive_num FROM neighbors WHERE num = prev_num AND num = next_num ORDER BY consecutive_num;
guided_example.explanation: Only rows that sit in the middle of a matching three-row sequence pass the filter. DISTINCT removes duplicates when a longer streak creates multiple matching middle rows.

practice.prompt: Return each number that appears at least three times consecutively.
practice.expected_query: WITH neighbors AS (SELECT num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs) SELECT DISTINCT num AS consecutive_num FROM neighbors WHERE num = prev_num AND num = next_num ORDER BY consecutive_num;

hints: Use one CTE to calculate prev_num and next_num.
A middle row qualifies when num = prev_num and num = next_num.
Use DISTINCT because long streaks can produce repeated answers.
